title: 📦 Nominalization

sections.heading: What is it?
sections.body:
Nominalization = turning verbs or adjectives into nouns. It's a key feature of academic writing that creates a denser, more formal style.

Verb → Noun:
decide → decision
analyse → analysis
improve → improvement
develop → development

Adjective → Noun:
accurate → accuracy
efficient → efficiency
complex → complexity

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.body:
Nominalization allows you to:
• Pack more information into fewer words
• Create noun phrases as subjects ("The analysis of data...")
• Avoid weak sentence structures
• Sound more academic and formal

Band 6: "The government decided to invest."
Band 8: "The government's decision to invest..."
Band 9: "The decision to substantially increase investment..."

highlight: Nominalization is a defining feature of academic writing. Band 9 essays nominalise frequently and naturally — without sounding forced.

example.wrong: When it rained heavily, the roads flooded and this caused many accidents.
example.right: The heavy rainfall resulted in severe flooding, leading to a significant increase in road accidents.

instruction: Match each verb to its correct nominalization:
explanation: These nominalisations appear constantly in academic writing. The ability to switch between verb and noun forms fluidly is a Band 8+ skill.

question: Which sentence uses nominalization most effectively for academic writing?
options: Researchers decided to investigate how students learn.
Research involved investigating how students learn.
The investigation of student learning strategies revealed key insights.
They investigated students and found some things out.
correct: The investigation of student learning strategies revealed key insights.
explanation:
✅ "The investigation of student learning strategies" = nominalization + of-phrase = formal, dense academic style

"Decided to investigate" and "involved investigating" still use verb forms
"They investigated...found some things out" = informal and vague

The nominalized version allows a clear, precise subject at the start of the sentence.
hint: Look for the option that turns the verb into a noun and uses an "of" phrase.

sentence: The _______ of greenhouse gas emissions has become a central concern for modern governments.
explanation:
"Reduction" is the nominalized form of "reduce".

The structure "The reduction of X" is a classic academic noun phrase — subject + of + noun phrase.

❌ "The reducing of" — gerund, less formal
❌ "The reduce of" — ungrammatical
❌ "The reduced of" — adjective, ungrammatical here
hint: Turn the verb "reduce" into a noun to fit "The ___ of..."

title: Nominalization Error
instruction: Find the sentence that misuses nominalization:

sentences.text: The implementation of this policy requires careful consideration.
The government made a decision of implementing the new tax.
sentences.explanation:
"Made a decision of implementing" is ungrammatical. The correct structures are:

✅ "made a decision to implement" (infinitive)
✅ "made the decision of implementation" (but awkward)
✅ "The government's decision to implement the new tax..." (best)

Nominalization doesn't mean stuffing nouns everywhere — the result must be grammatical and natural.

sentences.text: An increase in urban migration has led to significant housing shortages.
